content: Cefixime is indicated for the treatment of acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by susceptible isolates of Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. The recommended dosage is 400 mg per day, administered orally either as a single daily dose or divided into two doses every 12 hours. Cefixime is also indicated for the treatment of otitis media caused by susceptible isolates of Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Streptococcus pyogenes. The dosage remains 400 mg per day, given orally as a single daily dose or divided every 12 hours. For the treatment of pharyngitis and tonsillitis caused by susceptible isolates of Streptococcus pyogenes, cefixime should be administered at a dose of 400 mg per day, either as a single daily dose or divided every 12 hours. Treatment should continue for at least 10 days to ensure eradication of the infection. Cefixime may be used as an alternative treatment for uncomplicated urogenital, anorectal, or pharyngeal gonorrhea in cases where ceftriaxone is unavailable. However, it is no longer recommended as a first-line treatment according to CDC guidelines. The preferred regimen is 400 mg of cefixime orally once, combined with 1 g of azithromycin orally once. Alternatively, doxycycline 100 mg orally every 12 hours for 7 days may be used. For uncomplicated urinary tract infections caused by susceptible isolates of Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis, cefixime is administered at 400 mg per day, either as a single daily dose or divided every 12 hours. In pediatric patients weighing ≤45 kg, the dosage is 8 mg/kg/day, given as a single daily dose or divided every 12 hours. Safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 6 months of age. Cefixime is contraindicated in patients receiving live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine or cholera vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until the antibiotic course is completed. Similarly, the typhoid vaccine (live) should not be given to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Cefixime may decrease the efficacy of oral microbiota products, such as probiotics containing bacterial spores, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotic regimens should be completed 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. Cefixime can increase the nephrotoxic and/or ototoxic effects of aminoglycosides, such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, streptomycin, and tobramycin. Caution and close monitoring are advised when co-administering these agents. Similarly, co-administration with voclosporin may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. Cefixime may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors, such as atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab. Caution and monitoring are recommended during co-administration. Cefixime may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives, such as those containing ethinyl estradiol, dienogest, or levonorgestrel. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, additional or alternative forms of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. Cefixime may increase the levels or effects of acidic (anionic) drugs, such as aspirin, bendroflumethiazide, choline magnesium trisalicylate, cyclopenthiazide, meloxicam, and willow bark, by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is generally minor or unknown, but caution is advised. Cefixime may increase the anticoagulant effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Close monitoring of coagulation parameters is recommended during co-administration. Probenecid can increase the levels or effects of cefixime by competing for renal tubular clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised when these drugs are used together. Cefixime may increase the toxicity of furosemide through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of nephrotoxicity. Monitoring is recommended during co-administration. Chloramphenicol may antagonize the effects of cefixime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of cefixime by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown.
